Subject: Re: Observability for private deploy - initial constraints

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. Quick summary of our constraints so we can align the integration:
- We run in a locked-down VPC in AWS (no public IPs on compute).
- Outbound egress only via a customer-managed NAT/egress gateway; we cannot receive inbound connections.
- SIEM ingestion is Splunk HEC behind an internal load balancer (10.x.x.x) and requires mTLS with client certs + token header.
- All logs/metrics must stay in our account; we can accept a push-based forwarder that originates from our VPC to your forwarder endpoint in our account.
- Retention / audit: we need signed evidence of key rotation policy and access logs for the forwarder.

I've attached a short PDF that shows our egress firewall rules and the HEC cluster topology. Can your private package operate as a customer-managed forwarder (we run it in our ASG) and point to our internal HEC? If not, what alternatives do you support?

Thanks,
John
John Brennan

John —

Appreciate the clear constraints. Short answer: yes, we support both push-based customer-run forwarders (collector running in your VPC) and a lightweight agent that can POST to internal HEC endpoints. A couple of clarifying Qs before we produce a runbook:
1) Preferred transport: syslog (TLS), HTTP HEC with token header + mTLS, or a Fluent Bit/OTel collector pushing to your internal LB?
2) Cert management: can you issue short-lived client certs via your internal PKI (SCEP/ACME) or will you require us to provision long-lived client certs you upload?
3) Audit logs: which storage/service do you want the forwarder access logs sent to (CloudWatch Logs / S3 / Splunk index)? We can emit signed upload receipts and rotation proofs.

I've attached a sample HEC YAML (acme_hec_config.yaml) that shows the header + mTLS verification we expect your HEC to present for token validation on our side. It includes a placeholder token header X-Acme-Token.

Plan: after your answers we'll propose (A) forwarder-as-deployment (you run the collector in your ASG, forwards to internal HEC) and (B) an outbound-only proxy option where our package provides a one-way uploader that your ops runs and rotates creds locally.

Next steps: can we get a short call tomorrow 10:00 PT to confirm cert flow?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan

John / Tessa —

Adding some network-level specifics from the runtime/forwarder side so you can validate with networking:
- Forwarder placement: run on private subnets with an ENI in the same AZ as model-serving nodes to avoid cross-AZ egress charges.
- Egress: the forwarder will need outbound only https:443 to the internal LB (10.0.2.x) — no inbound. We support routing via NAT Gateway or VPC Endpoint (interface) if you prefer private link style connectivity.
- mTLS: our collector (Fluent Bit + custom plugin) supports client cert verification and will present a client cert chain if you provide the keypair. For improved security we can do mutual auth + rotate certs monthly.
- Token header: we can add X-Acme-Token and rotate it using your secrets manager; the forwarder can pull tokens from AWS Secrets Manager or Vault (we support both).
- Tracing hooks: the forwarder can attach trace_id/span_id metadata to log events. If you want distributed tracing exported to a local OpenTelemetry collector, we recommend running the otel-collector sidecar that receives Jaeger/OTLP from the runtime.

Technical snippet (for your firewall team):
curl -k --cert client.pem --key client.key --header 'X-Acme-Token: <REDACTED>' \
  https://10.0.2.12:8088/services/collector/event

If your HEC expects token-in-body instead of header we can adapt. Also: do you require client certs to be signed by your internal CA only (no public CA)?

-Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Confirming a few points from our side after reviewing the snippet and the PDF:
- HEC is internal-only (10.0.2.0/24). We'll add an inbound rule allowing your collector's outbound IP CIDR (we provide the ENI IP range for the ASG).
- Client certs must be signed by our internal CA and rotated at least every 90 days. We can provide short-lived certs via our SCEP endpoint (ops will coordinate).
- Token must be in header X-Acme-Token and validated on the HEC tier.
- Audit: we need the forwarder to write a signed manifest to an S3 bucket after each rotation with the old cert thumbprint + timestamp. That S3 bucket will be locked-down and cross-account read for our audit role.

Two items to validate before we spin up the POC:
1) Does Redwood's forwarder support writing signed manifests (we saw this mentioned in the docs)? If so we need the schema.
2) Are tracing exports limited to OTLP/Jaeger over gRPC or can you send traces over HTTP to our otel-collector?

We can approve a short-lived test cert for the POC once these are confirmed.

Regards,
Acme Security Team

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-06-15T11:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Observability for private deploy - initial constraints

Thanks — answers inline.

1) Signed manifests: yes, our forwarder supports a signed rotation manifest. Schema (summary):
- manifest_id (uuid)
- timestamp
- previous_cert_thumbprint
- new_cert_thumbprint
- signer_key_id
- signature (RSA-PSS base64)
We can push the manifest to S3 via your cross-account role or send it to your internal audit API. We'll include a sample manifest during the POC.

2) Traces: we support OTLP over gRPC and HTTP, Jaeger over UDP/TCP, and Zipkin. For an internal-only setup we usually recommend OTLP/gRPC to your otel-collector on 4317 (internal LB). If you prefer HTTP we can set otel in http/protobuf mode.

Sample otel-collector snippet (otel-sample-collector.conf):
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
      http:
exporters:
  logging:
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [logging]

Operational notes:
- The forwarder will tag logs with redwood.instance_id and redwood.runtime_version.
- We support a forwarder-only mode where telemetry is forwarded without any control-plane calls to Redwood (for air-gapped needs).
- For cert rotation we can integrate with your SCEP server: the forwarder can request new certs and atomically swap them, emitting the manifest to S3.

I'll upload the sample manifest and the otel config to the shared Drive link. Happy to run the POC once you issue a test cert.

—Mina
Senior Applied Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
